newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech coalition partner seeks budget concessions.
newsitem.headline: Czech coalition partner seeks budget concessions.

text.p: A junior partner of the Czech ruling coalition, the Civic Democratic Aliance (ODA), has conditioned support for the government's 1997 budget on a compromise on price deregulations, a spokesman said on Tuesday.

David Rozanek told Reuters that ODA, the most agressively pro-business partner in the three-party coalition would insist on a timetable for specific price deregulations and privatisations already in the coalition agreement.
"The condition for the budget's support is that we want to find a compromise...All we want is a discussion...a timetable that would direct the deregeulation," the spokesman said.

The coalition, led by the centre-right Civic Democratic Party (ODS) of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and the Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), lost its majority in the 200-seat lower chamber of the Parliamnt after summer general elections.
The coalition needs all the support it can muster to pass the budget in its final two readings in parliament later this month.
In the first reading in early October, four members of the strongest oppostion party, the Social Democrats (CSSD), broke party ranks to help the draft move to a second reading.
Senior representatives of ODS, KDU-CSL and ODA are expected to meet to discuss their budget strategies late on Tuesday.
Rozanek said he does not expect an immediate agreement.
"I do not think we would find the agreement today...there will have to be another meeting by the time the budget comes on the agenda of the Chamber."
The draft is expected to go to the floor of parliament early in this month's session starting on December 10.
